title: Memory footprint, leaks and jetsam
summary: iOS has no swap file. When memory runs low, the system kills apps (jetsam) - even the one on screen if it passes its limit. Keep memory low: small decoded images, bounded caches, no leaks.
body: **In simple words:** A Mac can move unused memory to disk. An iPhone cannot, so it simply kills apps that use too much. A killed foreground app looks like a crash to the user but produces **no crash report**.

**Clean vs dirty memory:** clean memory (app code, memory-mapped files) can be thrown away and reloaded. Dirty memory (objects you allocated, decoded images) cannot. Your "footprint" is mostly dirty + compressed memory, and that is what the limit counts.
**Biggest usual culprit - images:** a decoded image costs width × height × 4 bytes. A 12 MP photo ≈ 48 MB in memory regardless of a 2 MB JPEG file. Downsample to the size you display.
**Leaks vs growth:** a leak is memory no one can reach (retain cycles). Abandoned memory is still reachable but never used again (a cache that only grows). Both raise the footprint.

**Tools:** Xcode memory gauge, Memory Graph Debugger (cycles, who holds what), Instruments Allocations (mark generations: open and close a screen, see what remains) and Leaks; in production, MetricKit and Xcode Organizer (memory terminations).
**Reacting to pressure:** use `NSCache` (evicts automatically), clear custom caches on `didReceiveMemoryWarning`, and do not hold large data you can reload.
keyPoints: No swap on iOS: over the limit = jetsam kill, no crash log.
Footprint = dirty + compressed memory; images are usually the biggest part.
Decoded image = width × height × 4 bytes; always downsample.
Find leaks with Memory Graph, growth with Allocations generations.
Use `NSCache` with a cost limit; purge on memory warnings.

mistakes: Using a plain `Dictionary` as an image cache (never evicts).
Loading a full-resolution photo into a thumbnail-size view.
followups: **How do you detect out-of-memory crashes in production?** MetricKit/Organizer termination reasons; or infer: app was in foreground, no crash report, no clean exit on next launch.
**Why does memory keep growing in a feed?** Full-size decode per cell, unbounded caches, leaked cells or view controllers.
